title: L'IMAD (via ADQ) closes tender offer, lifting ownership of AD Ports Group above 98.5%
summary: Abu Dhabi sovereign investor L'IMAD, acting through its subsidiary ADQ, closed its voluntary cash offer for AD Ports Group on 15 September 2026, taking its stake from 75.4% to over 98.5%, with settlement due by 9 October 2026. The take-private frees AD Ports from public-market funding constraints and short-term return expectations, explicitly to pursue long-term investments and acquisitions. For DP World this means a state-backed rival with a deeper and more patient capital base for international concessions and M&A.

title: L'IMAD launches AED 6.25/share cash offer for the 24.58% of AD Ports Group it does not own
summary: L'IMAD Holding, Abu Dhabi's newest sovereign investor which took over ADQ's asset base in 2026, announced a voluntary conditional cash offer at AED 6.25 per share (23% premium) valuing AD Ports Group at AED 31.8bn (c. USD 8.7bn). AD Ports' board backed the offer on 26 August. The company at the time operated 40 terminals across c. 50 markets and had pending acquisitions in Brazil, Germany and Egypt.

title: AD Ports Group Q2 2026: record AED 836m net profit (+88%) despite 65% collapse in UAE container volumes from Hormuz disruption
summary: Q2 2026 revenue rose 47% to AED 7.08bn and net profit 88% to AED 836m, lifted by AED 650m of asset sales and a 62% jump in Maritime & Shipping revenue as Gulf-ISC freight rates rose 96%. UAE container throughput fell 65% to 573k TEU and bulk/general cargo fell 67% as the Strait of Hormuz conflict diverted traffic; AD Ports rerouted via Fujairah and Khor Fakkan with 27 container and 5 bulk vessels, 400 trucks and extra Etihad Rail frequencies. H1 2026 net profit was AED 1.49bn (+64%).
capacity: Q2 UAE throughput 573k TEU; feeder volumes 740k TEU

title: AD Ports raises Alexandria Container (ALCN) tender offer to EGP 27.47/share; Egyptian Transport Ministry reportedly set to reject
summary: Through subsidiary Black Caspian Logistics, AD Ports lifted its mandatory tender offer for up to 90% of Alexandria Container & Cargo Handling Co. by c. 19.5% to EGP 27.47 per share, having already built a 51.33% indirect majority. Egyptian state holders (Holding Company for Maritime & Land Transport 35.3%, Alexandria Port Authority 7.6%) hold a 42.9% blocking stake and a senior official said the ministry would reject the offer. Outcome determines whether AD Ports consolidates Egypt's largest Mediterranean container operator (Alexandria and El-Dekheila, 1.5m TEU capacity).
partners: Holding Company for Maritime & Land Transport

title: AD Ports Group acquires Brazil's CLI agri-bulk terminal operator for USD 835m, its largest-ever deal and first entry into Latin America
summary: AD Ports agreed to buy Corredor Logistica e Infraestrutura (CLI) from Macquarie Asset Management and IG4 Capital at an enterprise value of AED 3.1bn (USD 835m). CLI owns 100% of CLI Norte (grain terminal, Port of Itaqui) and 80% of CLI Sul (Brazil's leading sugar export terminal, Port of Santos), handling 17m tonnes in 2025 with revenue of USD 178m and EBITDA of USD 98m. The deal anchors AD Ports' agrifood vertical and a planned Brazil-Indian Subcontinent-East Africa-Khalifa Port grain corridor. Closing expected H2 2026 subject to antitrust approval.

title: AD Ports exercises call option to raise Global Feeder Shipping stake from 51% to 81% for AED 1.1bn
summary: AD Ports bought a further 30% of Dubai-based Global Feeder Shipping (GFS), the world's fourth-largest feeder operator by capacity, for AED 1.1bn (c. USD 300m) at the same AED 3.67bn enterprise value set when it acquired 51% in February 2024. GFS carried 2.8m TEU across 700+ voyages in 2025, serving 89 ports in 54 countries across the GCC, ISC, Red Sea, Far East, Mediterranean and Africa, and has generated over AED 1.8bn cumulative EBITDA since 2024. A direct competitor to Unifeeder, now firmly under AD Ports control.

title: AD Ports Group to acquire Germany's MBS Logistics for EUR 70m, gaining a Central European freight-forwarding platform
summary: AD Ports agreed to buy 100% of the core business of Cologne-area asset-light forwarder MBS Logistics at an enterprise value of AED 300m (EUR 70m / USD 79m). MBS had 2025 revenue of c. EUR 205m, 26 offices and 450+ staff, with operations in Germany, Central Europe, China, Vietnam and the US across air, ocean, road and rail forwarding, contract logistics and aerospace. Closing expected H2 2026 subject to EU approvals; it extends the Noatum Logistics network and competes with DP World Logistics in Europe.

title: AD Ports Group Q1 2026: net profit +41% to AED 653m; international container throughput +17% while UAE volumes fall 5%
summary: Q1 2026 revenue rose 25% to AED 5.75bn and EBITDA 33% to AED 1.52bn. Container feeder volumes grew 20% to 871k TEU and the bulk/MPP/Ro-Ro fleet reached 63 vessels. International container utilisation reached 65% versus 54% in the UAE. The quarter also saw a USD 2.5bn syndicated loan refinanced to March 2029, 843,000 sqm of new KEZAD land leases and a 450,000 sqm Metal Park launch in Abu Dhabi.

title: AD Ports Group named master planner and strategic partner for Al Selmiyyah Defence Industrial Free Zone in Abu Dhabi
summary: AD Ports Group signed a strategic partnership with the Tawazun Council for Defence Enablement to develop Al Selmiyyah, a dedicated defence manufacturing free zone in Abu Dhabi. AD Ports leads master planning, land use and infrastructure planning, while Tawazun handles regulatory and licensing frameworks. Delivery is phased; it extends KEZAD's model into a new sovereign-priority sector.

title: AD Ports reroutes feeder network via Fujairah and Khor Fakkan, adds land bridges and new ISC/Red Sea feeder loops during Hormuz closure
summary: Since late February 2026 AD Ports has rerouted SAFEEN Feeders and GFS services through Fujairah Terminals and Khor Fakkan on the Gulf of Oman, launched new feeder services linking India, Pakistan, Oman, the Red Sea and the Upper Gulf, and scaled a dedicated fleet to 24 container and bulk vessels. Around 54,000 TEU had been handled via the east-coast ports by mid-April, trucked through bonded corridors with 800 trucks and four extra daily Etihad Rail trips to Khalifa Port, Jebel Ali and Sharjah; essential-goods warehousing exceeded 76,000 sqm with plans to reach 188,000 sqm.
capacity: 24 dedicated vessels; ~54k TEU rerouted by Apr 2026

title: KEZAD Group signs five new industrial projects worth AED 147m across KEZAD Al Ain and Al Ma'mourah
summary: Five investors (Haber/Elixir oilfield chemicals, Grand Line Industries, Precent Enterprises metals coating, Unibal Group and Al Lul Transport) committed AED 147m across more than 84,000 sqm, creating c. 500 jobs. AED 47m goes to four projects in KEZAD Al Ain and AED 100m to a large industrial/logistics warehousing project in Al Ma'mourah. Illustrates the breadth of KEZAD's SME leasing pipeline competing with Jafza and DP World's Dubai zones.

title: KEZAD monetises 1 sq km Town Centre plot to Danube Properties for AED 840m and sells KLP warehouses to MAIR and Aldar
summary: In Q1 2026 AD Ports sold a 1.0 sq km KEZAD Town Centre plot to Danube Properties for AED 840m and three KLP Free Zone warehouses to MAIR Group for AED 295m, followed post-quarter by a sale of three KLP warehouses to Aldar for AED 650m. Together with the 2025 Mira Developments land sale (AED 2.47bn), this marks a shift to asset recycling in the Economic Cities & Free Zones cluster to fund international expansion while keeping leverage near 4x.

title: AD Ports Group FY2025: record AED 20.8bn revenue (+20%), AED 2.1bn net profit, 7.7m TEU throughput (+23%) and first positive FCF since IPO
summary: FY2025 EBITDA reached AED 5.1bn (24.4% margin) with cash from operations of AED 5.05bn and organic capex of AED 5.5bn; net debt was AED 20.6bn (4.1x). Group container throughput rose 23% to 7.7m TEU across 34 terminals, feeder volumes 38% to 3.35m TEU, and the bulk/MPP/Ro-Ro fleet grew from 28 to 60 vessels (largely via the UGR JV). CMA Terminals Khalifa Port handled 1.3m TEU in its first year at 74% utilisation; KEZAD leased 3.3 sq km net new land.
capacity: 7.7m TEU group throughput; 34 terminals; 3.35m TEU feeder volumes

title: AD Ports Group takes 51% effective interest in 30-year concession for new dry bulk terminal at Port of Douala, Cameroon
summary: AD Ports and two other UAE investors hold 60% of the operating company (AD Ports effective 51%) alongside Africa Ports Development (40%) under a 30-year concession with the Port Authority of Douala to design, build and operate a dry bulk terminal. Phase 1 (2026-2028) covers two berths and c. 450 m of quay with c. 4m tonnes/yr capacity for clinker, gypsum, fertiliser and grain; AD Ports' share of phase-1 capex is c. AED 320m (EUR 73.4m). It is AD Ports' second Central African gateway after Pointe-Noire and sits alongside the DP World-adjacent Douala market.

title: AD Ports Group signs 30-year concession to operate Aqaba Multipurpose Port, Jordan's only general cargo seaport
summary: AD Ports (70%) and Aqaba Development Corporation (30%) formed a JV to operate and upgrade the Aqaba Multipurpose Port under a 30-year concession, with AD Ports investing AED 141m (USD 38.4m) plus operating expertise. The port has nine berths, 2 km of quay and 13.5 m draft with 11m tonnes/yr capacity, handling 5.3m tonnes and c. 85,000 CEU of Ro-Ro imports in 2025. Operations were due to transfer in August 2026, giving AD Ports a Red Sea/Levant foothold next to DP World's Jeddah and Sokhna positions.

title: AD Ports secures USD 115m IFC-led, 15-year project financing for Noatum Ports Safaga Terminal on Egypt's Red Sea
summary: IFC led a USD 115m, 15-year project finance facility with NBK-Egypt and co-lenders under IFC's managed co-lending programme for the USD 200m Safaga multipurpose terminal, the first internationally operated terminal in Upper Egypt, developed under AD Ports' 30-year concession with the Red Sea Ports Authority. Financial close was expected in Q1 2026. Safaga competes for Upper Egypt and Red Sea cargo with DP World Sokhna.

title: Safeen Drydocks acquires 100% of Spain's Balenciaga Astilleros shipyard for EUR 11.2m to enter offshore-wind vessel building
summary: AD Ports' Safeen Drydocks (Noatum Maritime) bought the Basque shipyard Balenciaga, which has two drydocks, a 105 m slipway and 22,000+ sqm of automated fabrication, and is one of few Spanish yards able to build Service Operation Vessels for offshore wind farms. The deal supports AD Ports' clean-energy diversification alongside its Masdar partnership and places it near Northern European offshore wind clusters, competing with Drydocks World in the European offshore vessel segment.

title: KEZAD signs 50-year land lease with Jotun Abu Dhabi for AED 450m paints manufacturing facility in ICAD-Musaffah
summary: Jotun Abu Dhabi will invest AED 450m (c. USD 122m) in an 83,177 sqm manufacturing plant in ICAD-KEZAD Musaffah under a 50-year lease, relocating from a 22,000 sqm site and creating c. 200 jobs. A separate 50-year lease with Galadari Brothers' heavy equipment division (AED 75m) was signed in the same period. Shows KEZAD's success in anchoring multinational manufacturers against Dubai's free zones.

title: AD Ports Group forms 51%-owned integrated logistics JV with Pakistan's CEI Supply Chain
summary: AD Ports took a 51% stake in a JV with CEI Supply Chain (World Wide Group), a Pakistani forwarder with offices in Karachi, Lahore, Sialkot and Islamabad, to link its Karachi terminals to inland logistics for automotive, retail, FMCG and energy clients. The entity consolidates into AD Ports from Q1 2026 and complements its USD 295m commitment to the Karachi Gateway terminals, deepening its Pakistan platform versus DP World's Karachi (QICT) operations.

title: AD Ports Group and AVESTO Group establish 51/49 logistics joint venture in Tajikistan
summary: AD Ports (51%) and Tajik conglomerate AVESTO Group (49%) signed a shareholder agreement for a phased logistics JV starting as an asset-light freight forwarder with exclusive rights to manage freight for AVESTO's subsidiaries and serve third parties across Tajikistan. It extends AD Ports' Central Asia corridor play (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Georgia) into a landlocked market where DP World is also building its Middle Corridor network.

title: AD Ports announces mandatory tender offer at EGP 22.99/share to take majority control of Alexandria Container & Cargo Handling
summary: A month after buying 19.3% of ALCN, AD Ports announced a cash MTO for a further c. 32% at EGP 22.99 per share to reach majority ownership, with Egyptian government shareholders retaining their stakes and completion targeted for Q2 2026 subject to Egyptian approvals. The move seeks control of Egypt's largest Mediterranean container operator (c. 1.07m TEU in FY2025 across Alexandria and El-Dekheila).

title: KEZAD signs AED 1.1bn of land leases with India's Jindal SAW (seamless pipe plant) and Haldiram (first MENA food manufacturing hub)
summary: Jindal SAW Group will build a c. AED 1bn, 300,000 MTPA seamless pipe plant on 400,000 sqm in ICAD-KEZAD Musaffah (c. 1,000 jobs), and Haldiram Group will invest AED 150-200m in a 114,000 sqm manufacturing hub with up to 11 lines in KEZAD Al Ma'mourah (300+ jobs). Combined, over 514,000 sqm of new manufacturing space, strengthening KEZAD's India-corridor positioning versus Jafza.

title: AD Ports buys 19.3% of Alexandria Container & Cargo Handling from Saudi PIF's SEIC for EGP 13.2bn
summary: AD Ports acquired a 19.328% stake in ALCN, operator of the Alexandria and El-Dekheila container terminals (1.5m TEU combined capacity, c. 1.07m TEU throughput and 71% utilisation in FY2025), from the Saudi Egyptian Investment Company for about EGP 13.2bn (c. USD 275m), funded from cash and debt. The block trade was the first step toward control and gives AD Ports a direct presence on the East-West corridor in Egypt's main Mediterranean gateway.

title: AD Ports Group agrees USD 22m deal with CMA CGM for 20% of Latakia International Container Terminal, Syria
summary: AD Ports signed a joint venture and shareholders' agreement with CMA CGM Group to take a 20% minority stake in Latakia International Container Terminal (LICT) for USD 22m (AED 81m). LICT handles c. 250,000 TEU, about 95% of Syria's container volumes, and targets 625,000 TEU capacity by end-2026. The entry puts AD Ports in Syria's main container gateway just months after DP World signed its USD 800m, 30-year Tartus concession.

title: Karachi Gateway Terminals award Van Oord dredging contract to deepen berths and lift KGTL capacity to 1m TEU
summary: AD Ports' Karachi Gateway Terminal (KGTL, containers) and KGTML (bulk/general cargo), both JVs with Kaheel Terminals led by Noatum Ports, contracted Van Oord to deepen berths and channels so vessels of 305-350 m and 13-15.5 m draft can call. KGTL capacity rises from 750k to 1m TEU and KGTML's maximum bulk parcel doubles from 60k to 120k tonnes, with works due Q1 2026. Part of c. USD 300m AD Ports is investing in Karachi infrastructure and digital systems, directly challenging DP World's QICT.
capacity: KGTL 750k -> 1m TEU; bulk vessels up to 120k t

title: AD Ports and Ningbo Zhoushan Port Group sign preliminary agreement for China-Middle East-Africa automotive logistics ecosystem
summary: At the maiden voyage of the 7,000 CEU LNG-powered car carrier UGR Zakher in Ningbo, AD Ports and Zhejiang Provincial Seaport Investment & Operation Group agreed to develop Ro-Ro and automotive terminals at Ningbo Zhoushan and AD Ports hubs, digital visibility platforms and sea-rail Middle Corridor routing, with United Global Ro-Ro (AD Ports/Erkport JV) as designated carrier. Targets Chinese EV export flows to the Gulf, Central Asia and Africa, a segment DP World also pursues at Jebel Ali and Sokhna.

title: AD Ports commits USD 775m to Kazakhstan: Sarzha multipurpose terminal JV at Kuryk, Caspian container ships with KazMunayGas
summary: At the UAE-Kazakhstan Business Forum in Astana, AD Ports signed heads of terms with SEMURG Invest for a JV to design, finance and operate the Sarzha Multipurpose Terminal at Kuryk Port (general cargo, containers, dry bulk) alongside an existing grain terminal JV, an agreement with KazMunayGas to commission up to four 780 TEU shallow-draft Caspian container ships (and consider four Aframax tankers), and trade MoUs with Kazakh Invest and SEZ Morport Aktau. AD Ports had invested USD 175m to date with c. USD 600m of further projects planned, positioning against DP World's Aktau/Kuryk and Middle Corridor ventures.

title: Noatum Maritime takes delivery of first LNG-powered 7,000 CEU PCTC for United Global Ro-Ro JV with Erkport
summary: UGR Al Samha, a 12-deck, 59,331 sqm LNG-fuelled pure car and truck carrier with capacity above 7,000 CEU, was delivered to Noatum Maritime for the United Global Ro-Ro joint venture with Turkey's Erkport, serving Middle East, Asia and Mediterranean routes. The UGR JV drove AD Ports' bulk/MPP/Ro-Ro fleet from 28 to 60 vessels during 2025, making AD Ports a sizeable short-sea and deep-sea Ro-Ro carrier in its own right.

title: AD Ports' talks to acquire a stake in Izmir Alsancak port collapse; Turkey turns to local investors
summary: Negotiations begun in late 2023 for AD Ports to take a stake in Izmir's Alsancak port in a reported USD 500m transaction fell through around February 2025. In August 2025 Turkish Transport Minister Uraloglu said the government was now seeking Turkish investors (possibly with foreign partners) for the operating rights, leaving AD Ports out of the picture. A setback for its Mediterranean/Black Sea strategy where DP World (Yarimca, Evyap) remains established.
partners: Turkish Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure

title: AD Ports starts operations at Noatum Ports Luanda Terminal and Noatum Unicargas Logistics JV in Angola
summary: AD Ports began operating the Luanda multipurpose terminal on 30 January 2025 under its 20-year concession (extendable 10 years) with the Luanda Port Authority, and started trading at Noatum Unicargas Logistics. AD Ports holds 81% of the terminal JV (with Unicargas and Multiparques) and 90% of the logistics JV; it committed c. USD 250m through 2026, rising to up to USD 380m, to upgrade the 192,000 sqm terminal to handle 14,000 TEU vessels, general cargo and Ro-Ro. Luanda handles c. 76% of Angola's container and general cargo, a market DP World also entered via Multiterminais.

title: AD Ports completes acquisition of 60% of Tbilisi Dry Port, Georgia's Middle Corridor intermodal hub
summary: AD Ports closed its purchase of a 60% stake in the Tbilisi Dry Port, a three-phase intermodal hub due to open in October 2024 with initial capacity of 96,500 TEU, 10,000 sqm of warehousing and a car yard, rising to 286,000 TEU and 100,000 sqm of warehousing at full build. It gives AD Ports a rail-connected inland node on the Trans-Caspian Middle Corridor between its Caspian (Kazakhstan) and Black Sea ambitions, competing with DP World's corridor initiatives.

title: AD Ports wins 15-year concession to manage cruise terminals at Safaga, Hurghada and Sharm El Sheikh
summary: Egypt's Red Sea Ports Authority awarded AD Ports Group a 15-year concession to manage and operate three cruise terminals at Safaga, Hurghada and Sharm El Sheikh, with AD Ports investing c. USD 4.7m; the terminals were expected to open in 2025. Builds on the Abu Dhabi Cruise Terminal model and the Safaga multipurpose terminal concession, extending AD Ports' Red Sea footprint.

title: East Africa Gateway (Adani, AD Ports, East Harbour Terminals) wins 30-year concession for Container Terminal 2 at Dar es Salaam
summary: East Africa Gateway Limited, a JV including Adani International Ports Holdings, AD Ports Group and East Harbour Terminals, signed a 30-year concession to operate Container Terminal 2 (berths 8-11) at Dar es Salaam, and acquired 95% of incumbent TICTS for USD 39.5m. The deal placed AD Ports in East Africa's key gateway alongside DP World's own 2023 Dar es Salaam concession (berths 0-7), making the port a head-to-head arena for the two UAE groups.

title: AD Ports signs 20-year concession to operate and upgrade Luanda multipurpose terminal with Unicargas and Multiparques
summary: AD Ports Group signed a 20-year concession (extendable by 10 years) with the Luanda Port Authority to operate and modernise the Luanda multipurpose terminal in partnership with Angolan state logistics firm Unicargas and Multiparques, committing c. USD 250m through 2026 and up to USD 380m over the term. The terminal is to handle containers, general cargo and Ro-Ro for Angola's largest port, with a related logistics JV. Positions AD Ports directly against DP World's Luanda Multiterminais operation.

title: AD Ports signs preliminary JV agreement with General Company for Ports of Iraq to develop Al-Faw Grand Port and economic zone
summary: Building on a 2021 MoU and 2023 addendum, AD Ports Group and the General Company for Ports of Iraq signed a preliminary agreement to form a JV to develop, finance, operate and maintain the Al-Faw Grand Port and its economic zone, potentially extending to ports and zones in other Iraqi cities, with feasibility studies to follow. No values disclosed. Al-Faw is the anchor of Iraq's Development Road corridor to Turkey, a strategic prize also of interest to DP World.
partners: General Company for Ports of Iraq

title: AD Ports and Kaheel win 25-year concession for Karachi Port East Wharf bulk and general cargo terminal (berths 11-17)
summary: Following its June 2023 container terminal concession (berths 6-10), AD Ports Group signed a 25-year concession with Karachi Port Trust to operate the bulk and general cargo terminal at East Wharf berths 11-17 through Karachi Gateway Terminal Multipurpose Ltd, a JV majority-owned by AD Ports with Kaheel Terminals. Investment of c. USD 75m in the first two years and a further USD 100m within five years aims to lift capacity by 75% to up to 14m tonnes/yr (steel, paper, clinker, grains, fertiliser).

title: Noatum closes EUR 81m acquisition of Spain's Sesé Auto Logistics, creating Noatum Auto Logistics
summary: AD Ports' Noatum completed the 100% acquisition of Sesé Auto Logistics, a Spanish finished-vehicle logistics firm with 200+ trucks operating across Spain, Germany, Poland, Czechia and Hungary, for EUR 81m, rebranding it Noatum Auto Logistics. Combined with Noatum's Ro-Ro terminals and the UGR car-carrier JV, it gives AD Ports an end-to-end European automotive logistics chain.

title: Noatum Terminals completes acquisition of APM Terminals Castellón from Maersk's APMT for EUR 10m
summary: Noatum Terminals (AD Ports Group) closed the purchase of 100% of APM Terminals Castellón at a EUR 10m enterprise value, consolidating its position in Castellón where it has run a multipurpose terminal since 2004. The combined 250,000 sqm site has 250,000 TEU/yr capacity (c. 70% of the port's container capacity), 2m tonnes of bulk handling, Ro-Ro and direct rail links. APMT said the asset no longer fitted its strategy.
